caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1176 of 2005.
lawyer:
Harendra Nath Nondi, Advocate instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Not represented— Respondents.
parties:
Hari Thakur Deb Bigraha ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Md. Abdul Hannan ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 215 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rajshahi for declaration that the plaintiff has already acquired good and indefeasible title in the suit land as described in schedule 'B', a part of the schedule 'A' of the plaint, by adverse possession for more than long 12 years in respect of 0.1164 acres of land with all pucca houses thereon appertaining to CS Khatian No. 517, SA Khatian No. 504, RS Khatian No. 552 corresponding to CS Plot No. 816, SA Plot No. 1250 and RS Plot Nos. 4080 and 4081 out of 0.1687 acres situated within Mouza Seriol, PS Boalia District Rajshahi. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the property originally belonged to one Moni Dasi who established a family deity Sree Hari Thakur Deb Bigraha to her said house and constituted herself as the Shebait of the said deity and accordingly, during CS operation, the entire land mentioned in schedule A to the plaint was recorded as such. Shebait Moni Dasi died childless and, according to her oral direction the Brahmin Porohit, Jotish Chandra Chakraborty, became the Shebait for the said debuttar property. Shebait Jotish Chandra Chakraborty died leaving behind his two sons namely Lakshmi Narayan Chakraborty and Rajeswar Chakraborty and only daughter Charushila Rani Chakraborty and all of them have been living in the said house situated on the 'A' schedule property. Subsequently, Rajeshwar Chakraborty, the youngest son of Jotish Chandra Chakraborty, who is the present plaintiff, embraced Islam in 1962 and adopted the Islamic name Md. Abdul Hannan. In view of such conversion of the plaintiff, a very strained relationship cropped up between the plaintiff and the members of his parents' family. The plaintiff also removed the said deity from the "Thakur Ghar" situated on the suit plot. The plaintiff is in continuous peaceful possession in the suit land and the existence of the deity completely ceased. While the plaintiff had been in possession of the said land of schedule 'B', the liberation war started in the year 1971 when his parents and elder brother, the defendant No. 5 embraced Islam but his father was lifted away and killed by the Pak Army and his dead body could not be traced out. Thereafter, the plaintiff's mother died as a Muslim in 1976 and she was buried in the suit plot. The plaintiff and his elder brother Lakshimi Narayan Chakraborty who also on embracing Islam adopted the Islamic name of Abdur Razzaque, remained in possession of the suit plot in their specific portion. The plaintiff has been paying municipal taxes separately for his portion as a separate holding. The plaintiff's elder brother Abdur Razzaque, the defendant No. 5, renounced Islam in 1982 and adopted his original name Lakshimi Narayan to grab the entire property. The plaintiff's elder brother himself filed a case before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Paba, Bollia Circle Rajshahi for mutation of his name in respect of the entire suit plot as Shebait but on objection raised by the plaintiff, the said mutation proceeding was dropped. Thereafter the said elder brother instigated and set up other persons to file a petition before the ADC (Rev), Rajshahi on 18-7-1985 on false claim to appoint a Shebait of the 'A' schedule land treating the same to be public debuttar property of the Hindu people in general. As a result, a cloud was cast upon the title of the plaintiff. Hence is the suit.
